options: Any hardware on which data is stored
Anything that generates data for decision-making which ultimately generates revenue for the organisation
Datasets that are kept purely for compliance
Data that is not currently in use
The licences a company holds for its databases
questions.explanation: Data Assets are anything that generates data for decision-making and, through that, generates revenue for the organisation.

questions.stem: Which three artefacts, the "3 Ds", have Data Assets as their perfect business case?
options: Data Lake, Delta Lake and Data Vault
Data Mining, Data Science and Deep Learning
Data Drift, Data Detritus and Dark Data
Data Catalog, Data Dictionary and Data Glossary
questions.explanation: Data Assets justify having a Data Catalog, Data Dictionary and Data Glossary, because one must know what the data is about and where it resides.

questions.stem: Why do Data Assets require a Data Catalog, Data Dictionary and Data Glossary?
options: Because one must know what the data is all about and where it is residing
Because regulators require all three documents
Because they replace the need for a data warehouse
Because they reduce storage costs automatically
questions.explanation: To treat data as an asset, an organisation must know what each dataset is about and where it lives, which is what the three Ds provide.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as an example of a Data Asset in a data-driven company?
questions.explanation: The examples given are systems, websites, portals, mobile applications, output Excel files, dashboards, reports and campaigns; server racks are not listed.

questions.stem: Which companies are given as the best examples of businesses that run on their data as an asset?
questions.explanation: Facebook, Google and Twitter are cited as the best examples of companies using their data as an asset to run their businesses.

questions.stem: Which action is named as a way to maintain Data Assets by cutting the cost of data management?
options: Moving all data to the operational database
Storing every dataset in a single format
questions.explanation: One way to maintain Data Assets is to cut the cost of data management by deleting or purging unnecessary data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the stated ways to maintain Data Assets?
options: Make maximum value by selling data to generate revenue
Keep multiple uncontrolled copies of every dataset
Cut the cost of data management by purging unnecessary data
questions.explanation: The ways listed are cutting cost, generating revenue, managing the Data Catalog, and protection and security; keeping uncontrolled copies is not among them.

questions.stem: In a nutshell, which datasets count as Data Assets?
options: Datasets that are stored on the most expensive hardware
Datasets which have ROI and are able to generate revenue
Datasets that have never been accessed
Datasets held only for audit purposes
Datasets that are larger than one terabyte
questions.explanation: The summary definition is that Data Assets are datasets which have a return on investment and are able to generate revenue.

questions.stem: For which type of company are Data Assets described as the most valuable artefacts?
questions.explanation: For data-driven companies, Data Assets are the most valuable artefacts, spanning systems, portals, reports, campaigns and more.

questions.stem: What does "make maximum value out of" a Data Asset mean in practice?
options: Convert it to a single file format
questions.explanation: Making maximum value out of Data Assets is described as selling the data to generate revenue.
